questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. If (P) has an optimal solution with optimal value $Z^{\ast}$, what follows for (D)?
options: (D) has an optimal solution, with optimal value at least $Z^{\ast}$, possibly larger
(D) is feasible, but it need not have an optimal solution
(D) has an optimal solution, with optimal value equal to $Z^{\ast}$
(D) has an optimal solution or is infeasible; (P) alone does not decide

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. It is known only that (D) has a feasible solution. Which outcomes of (P) are still possible?
options: Only an optimal solution, since a feasible (D) bounds the objective of (P)
An optimal solution or infeasibility; only 'unbounded' is ruled out
An optimal solution or unboundedness; only 'infeasible' is ruled out
All three outcomes, since nothing is known about (P) itself

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. Suppose (P) is infeasible. What follows for (D)?
options: (D) is unbounded, since nothing in (P) bounds its objective from below
(D) is infeasible, since infeasibility carries over from (P) to (D)
(D) has an optimal solution or is unbounded, depending on $\boldsymbol{c}$
(D) is unbounded or infeasible, and each case occurs for suitable data

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. Which list gives exactly the pairs (outcome of (P), outcome of (D)) that can occur?
options: (optimal, optimal), (unbounded, infeasible), (infeasible, unbounded), (infeasible, infeasible)
(optimal, optimal), (unbounded, infeasible), (infeasible, unbounded)
(optimal, optimal), (unbounded, unbounded), (infeasible, infeasible)
(optimal, optimal), (unbounded, infeasible), (infeasible, unbounded), (unbounded, unbounded)

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. Why can (P) and (D) not both be unbounded?
options: Their optimal values would be $+\infty$ and $-\infty$, contradicting equal optimal values
A primal–dual pair always has two different outcomes, so both cannot be unbounded
A feasible point of (D) would give an upper bound on the objective of (P), by weak duality
Every feasible pair has $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$, so both objectives must stay finite

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max Z=x_1+2x_2$ subject to $-x_1+x_2\leq1$, $x_1-2x_2\leq2$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, whose dual (D) has the constraints $-y_1+y_2\geq1$, $y_1-2y_2\geq2$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. For every $t\geq0$ the point $(2t,t)$ is feasible for (P), with $Z=4t$. What is the outcome of (D)?
options: (D) is infeasible, since no single value $W$ can exceed $4t$ for all $t$
(D) is unbounded, since $Z=4t$ has no upper bound either
(D) is unbounded or infeasible; its constraints must be checked first
(D) has the optimal solution $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$, with optimal value $W^{\ast}=0$

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max Z=x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\leq-3$, $x_2\leq2$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=-3y_1+2y_2$ subject to $y_1\geq1$, $-y_1+y_2\geq1$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. Which combination of outcomes does this pair have?
options: (P) and (D) are both infeasible
(P) is unbounded and (D) is infeasible
(P) is infeasible and (D) has an optimal solution
(P) is infeasible and (D) is unbounded

questions.question: For (P) $\max Z=x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\leq2$, $-x_1+2x_2\leq2$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=2y_1+2y_2$ subject to $y_1-y_2\geq1$, $-y_1+2y_2\geq1$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$, a student reports: (P) is unbounded along $(2+t,t)$, $t\geq0$, and $\boldsymbol{y}=(3,2)$ is feasible for (D). What is correct?
options: Both reports can be right, since weak duality compares only the optimal values of (P) and (D)
They cannot both be right: $\boldsymbol{y}=(3,2)$ is feasible, so $Z\leq10$ and the ray fails
The ray report is right, so (D) is infeasible and $\boldsymbol{y}=(3,2)$ must violate a constraint
Both reports can be right, with (D) unbounded as well, since the two programs share an outcome

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max Z=x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq4$, $-x_1+x_2\leq-1$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=4y_1-y_2$ subject to $y_1-y_2\geq1$, $y_1+y_2\geq2$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. Which points prove, without solving either program, that (P) has an optimal solution?
options: $\boldsymbol{x}=(2,1)$ and $\boldsymbol{x}=(3,0)$, both feasible for (P)
$\boldsymbol{y}=(2,0)$ and $\boldsymbol{y}=(3,1)$, both feasible for (D)
$\boldsymbol{x}=(2,1)$ feasible for (P) and $\boldsymbol{y}=(2,0)$ feasible for (D)
$\boldsymbol{x}=(3,0)$ feasible for (P) and $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,1)$ feasible for (D)

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max Z=x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-2x_2\leq-2$, $-x_1+2x_2\leq1$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=-2y_1+y_2$ subject to $y_1-y_2\geq1$, $-2y_1+2y_2\geq1$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. What are the outcomes of (P) and of (D)?
options: (P) is infeasible and (D) is unbounded
(P) and (D) are both infeasible
(P) is unbounded and (D) is infeasible
(P) is infeasible; these data leave (D) open between unbounded and infeasible

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. Which result rules out that (P) has an optimal solution while (D) is infeasible?
options: Weak duality, since $Z^{\ast}$ is a lower bound for every value $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ of (D)
The fact that every linear program is infeasible, unbounded or has an optimal solution
The dual of the dual, since (D) must then share the outcome of its own dual (P)
Strong duality, since an optimal solution of (P) forces an optimal solution of (D)

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and (D) its dual. Weak duality gives: if (P) is unbounded, then (D) is infeasible. How does 'if (D) is unbounded, then (P) is infeasible' follow from this statement?
options: Apply it to (D) rewritten as a maximization; the dual of that program has the feasible set of (P)
It is the contrapositive of the statement for (P) and (D), so it follows by logic alone
It is the converse of the statement for (P) and (D), and converses of duality results hold too
By strong duality: an unbounded (D) has no optimal solution, so (P) is infeasible

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. The feasible region of (P) is nonempty and bounded. What holds for (D) for every $\boldsymbol{c}$?
options: (D) has a bounded feasible region as well, by the symmetry of the pair
(D) has an optimal solution, with the same optimal value as (P)
(D) is unbounded for some $\boldsymbol{c}$, because its feasible region is unbounded
(D) is feasible only when $\boldsymbol{c}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$, the case in which $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$ is feasible

questions.question: For a real parameter $\beta$, let (P) be $\max Z=2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\leq\beta$, $-2x_1+2x_2\leq-6$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=\beta y_1-6y_2$ subject to $y_1-2y_2\geq2$, $-y_1+2y_2\geq1$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. Which outcomes occur, depending on $\beta$?
options: $\beta\geq3$: (P) unbounded, (D) infeasible; $\beta<3$: (P) infeasible, (D) unbounded
$\beta>3$: (P) unbounded, (D) infeasible; $\beta\leq3$: both infeasible
$\beta\geq3$: (P) unbounded, (D) infeasible; $\beta<3$: both infeasible
$\beta\geq3$: both have optimal solutions; $\beta<3$: both infeasible

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max Z=2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\leq3$, $-x_1\leq-2$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=3y_1-2y_2$ subject to $y_1-y_2\geq2$, $-y_1\geq1$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. (D) is infeasible, since $-y_1\geq1$ contradicts $y_1\geq0$. What is the outcome of (P)?
options: (P) is infeasible, because $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ violates $-x_1\leq-2$
(P) is unbounded or infeasible, and these data cannot decide which
(P) has an optimal solution, since $2\leq x_1\leq3$ on its feasible region
(P) is unbounded, because $(2,0)$ is feasible for (P)

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max Z=-2x_1-x_2$ subject to $x_1-3x_2\leq4$, $-x_1+x_2\leq5$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=4y_1+5y_2$ subject to $y_1-y_2\geq-2$, $-3y_1+y_2\geq-1$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. Which outcomes, with optimal values $Z^{\ast}$ and $W^{\ast}$ where they exist, does this pair have?
options: Both have optimal solutions, with $Z^{\ast}=W^{\ast}=0$
(P) has $Z^{\ast}=0$, and (D) is unbounded because its feasible region is unbounded
(P) is unbounded because its feasible region is unbounded, and (D) is infeasible
Both have optimal solutions; $Z^{\ast}=0$, while $W^{\ast}>0$ still has to be computed

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. (P) is infeasible and the objective is $\boldsymbol{c}=\boldsymbol{0}$. What is the outcome of (D)?
options: (D) has the optimal solution $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$, with optimal value $0$
(D) is unbounded, since $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$ is feasible and (D) cannot be optimal
(D) is infeasible, since an infeasible (P) comes with an infeasible (D)
(D) is unbounded or infeasible, depending on $\boldsymbol{A}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and (D) its dual. (P) is unbounded. Keep $\boldsymbol{A}$ and $\boldsymbol{c}$ and replace $\boldsymbol{b}$ by any $\boldsymbol{b}'$. What holds for every such new primal?
options: The new primal is unbounded, since the unbounded direction does not involve $\boldsymbol{b}$
The new primal is unbounded or optimal, since a smaller $\boldsymbol{b}'$ can cut off the unbounded direction
The new primal can have any of the three outcomes, since each $\boldsymbol{b}'$ gives a new program
The new primal is unbounded or infeasible, never optimal, since its dual stays infeasible

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max Z=c_1x_1+c_2x_2$ subject to $2x_1-x_2\leq-1$, $-2x_1+x_2\leq0$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, which is infeasible, with dual (D) $\min W=-y_1$ subject to $2y_1-2y_2\geq c_1$, $-y_1+y_2\geq c_2$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. For exactly which $(c_1,c_2)$ are (P) and (D) both infeasible?
options: Exactly when $c_1+2c_2>0$
Exactly when $c_1+2c_2\geq0$
Exactly when $2c_1+c_2>0$
For no $(c_1,c_2)$, since an infeasible (P) has an unbounded (D)

questions.question: For real parameters $\beta$ and $k$, let (P) be $\max Z=x_1+kx_2$ subject to $x_1-2x_2\leq\beta$, $-x_1+2x_2\leq-2$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with dual (D) $\min W=\beta y_1-2y_2$ subject to $y_1-y_2\geq1$, $-2y_1+2y_2\geq k$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. For which $(\beta,k)$ is (P) infeasible and (D) unbounded?
options: Exactly when $\beta<2$ and $k>-2$
Exactly when $\beta\geq2$ and $k>-2$
Exactly when $\beta<2$ and $k\leq-2$
Exactly when $\beta<2$ and $k<-2$
